claims.source: The remaining 19/32 transcripts showed the majority of loss beyond 48 hr post-irradiation, consistent with being late progeny markers (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Based on time-course WISH analysis after irradiation.

claims.claim: All WThighXlow genes grouped as late progeny and were the only genes with detectable expression at 7 days post-irradiation.
claims.source: Interestingly, all WThighXlow genes grouped as late progeny, and moreover, were the only genes with detectable expression at 7 days post-irradiation.
claims.evidence: Based on irradiation time-course WISH analysis.

claims.claim: 7.2% ± 2.1 of prog-1+ cells were piwi-1+.
claims.source: Congruent with previous studies, we found a small amount of overlap between piwi-1 with prog-1, and minimal with AGAT-1: 7.2% ± 2.1 of prog-1+ cells were piwi-1+, while merely 0.29% ± 0.50 of AGAT-1+ cells were piwi-1+ (Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH quantification experiments.

claims.claim: 0.29% ± 0.50 of AGAT-1+ cells were piwi-1+.
claims.source: Congruent with previous studies, we found a small amount of overlap between piwi-1 with prog-1, and minimal with AGAT-1: 7.2% ± 2.1 of prog-1+ cells were piwi-1+, while merely 0.29% ± 0.50 of AGAT-1+ cells were piwi-1+ (Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH quantification experiments.

claims.claim: Only 5.4% ± 2.4 of prog-1+ cells co-expressed low levels of AGAT-1.
claims.source: In contrast to a previous study that found nearly 45% overlap between the progeny populations (Eisenhoffer et al., 2008), we found that only 5.4% ± 2.4 of prog-1+ cells co-expressed low levels of AGAT-1, while 5.2% ± 3.2 of AGAT-1+ cells had prog-1 expression.
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH quantification experiments, contrasting with previous findings.

claims.claim: 5.2% ± 3.2 of AGAT-1+ cells had prog-1 expression.
claims.source: In contrast to a previous study that found nearly 45% overlap between the progeny populations (Eisenhoffer et al., 2008), we found that only 5.4% ± 2.4 of prog-1+ cells co-expressed low levels of AGAT-1, while 5.2% ± 3.2 of AGAT-1+ cells had prog-1 expression.
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH quantification experiments.

claims.claim: 17.8% ± 12.2 of prog-1+ cells were PIWI-1+.
claims.source: In support of these data, we found that 17.8% ± 12.2 of prog-1+ cells to be PIWI-1+, while 1.6% ± 1.2 of AGAT-1+ cells had detectable PIWI-1 expression (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH with PIWI-1 immunolabeling.

claims.claim: 1.6% ± 1.2 of AGAT-1+ cells had detectable PIWI-1 expression.
claims.source: In support of these data, we found that 17.8% ± 12.2 of prog-1+ cells to be PIWI-1+, while 1.6% ± 1.2 of AGAT-1+ cells had detectable PIWI-1 expression (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH with PIWI-1 immunolabeling.

claims.claim: Almost all newly identified late progeny transcripts examined exhibited substantial co-expression with AGAT-1, with overlap ranging from 100% with prog-1-7 to 55.5% with prog-1-4.
claims.source: Almost all newly identified late progeny transcripts examined were found to exhibit substantial co-expression with AGAT-1, with overlap ranging from 100% with prog-1-7 to 55.5% with prog-1-4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH co-localization analysis.

claims.claim: Every new epithelial progenitor marker assessed was down-regulated after zfp-1 RNAi.
claims.source: We observed that every new epithelial progenitor marker assessed was down-regulated after zfp-1 RNAi, confirming that these genes were indeed expressed in epithelial progenitors (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: Based on WISH analysis in zfp-1 RNAi animals.

claims.claim: RNAi against prog-1 and prog-2 separately or together did not yield any detectable phenotype.
claims.source: In agreement with previous data, RNAi against prog-1 and prog-2 separately or together did not yield any detectable phenotype (Eisenhoffer et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Based on RNAi screening experiments, consistent with previous findings.

claims.claim: None of the new epithelial progenitor markers yielded phenotypes upon knockdown.
claims.source: Unexpectedly, none of the new epithelial progenitor markers yielded phenotypes upon knockdown either, suggestive of considerable functional redundancy among these genes.
claims.evidence: Based on RNAi screening experiments.

claims.claim: mex3-1(RNAi) was completely penetrant and lethal, resulting in ventral curling, head regression, and dorsal lesioning during homeostasis.
claims.source: mex3-1(RNAi) was completely penetrant and lethal, resulting in ventral curling, head regression, and dorsal lesioning during homeostasis, as well as loss of regenerative ability after amputation (Figure 3A–C), indicative of epithelial homeostasis defects as well as overall stem cell impairment (Bardeen and Baetjer, 1904; Reddien et al., 2005a).
claims.evidence: Based on phenotypic observations of mex3-1 RNAi animals.

claims.claim: mex3-1(RNAi) animals lost regenerative ability after amputation.
claims.source: mex3-1(RNAi) was completely penetrant and lethal, resulting in ventral curling, head regression, and dorsal lesioning during homeostasis, as well as loss of regenerative ability after amputation (Figure 3A–C), indicative of epithelial homeostasis defects as well as overall stem cell impairment (Bardeen and Baetjer, 1904; Reddien et al., 2005a).
claims.evidence: Based on regeneration assays shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Two other MEX3 homologs in S. mediterranea (mex3-2 and mex3-3) were neither irradiation-sensitive nor produced observable phenotypes after knockdown.
claims.source: Using reciprocal BLAST, we identified two other MEX3 homologs in S. mediterranea (mex3-2 and mex3-3, transcripts SmedASXL_000637 and SmedASXL_01505, respectively), which both contained two KH RNA-binding domains and had top reciprocal BLAST hits in mouse, fly, and C. elegans. These additional MEX3 homologs were neither irradiation-sensitive nor produced observable phenotypes after knockdown and thus not investigated further (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Based on RNAseq data and RNAi experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: mex3-1 showed >fivefold enrichment in the X2 fraction over irradiated worms but also exhibited significant expression in the X1 stem cell fraction.
claims.source: By RNAseq, mex3-1 showed >fivefold enrichment in the X2 fraction over irradiated worms but also exhibited significant expression in the X1 stem cell fraction (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: Based on RNAseq quantification shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: mex3-1 was widely expressed in stem cells, early progeny, and late progeny.
claims.source: Analysis of mex3-1 using dFISH with lineage markers confirmed that mex3-1 was widely expressed in stem cells, early progeny, and late progeny (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH co-localization analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: Knockdown of mex3-1 leads to a rapid decline of the two progeny populations but not of stem cells.
claims.source: Knockdown of mex3-1 leads to a rapid decline of the two progeny populations but not of stem cells (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), with the majority of progeny gene expression lost by 6 days after RNAi (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Based on WISH time-course analysis shown in Figure 4A and supplements.

claims.claim: The majority of progeny gene expression was lost by 6 days after mex3-1 RNAi.
claims.source: Knockdown of mex3-1 leads to a rapid decline of the two progeny populations but not of stem cells (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), with the majority of progeny gene expression lost by 6 days after RNAi (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Based on detailed time-course WISH analysis.

claims.claim: mex3-1(RNAi) animals had comparable levels of cell death to control worms up until 9 days after RNAi, but significantly higher levels from 12 days and onward.
claims.source: Quantification of TUNEL showed that mex3-1(RNAi) animals had comparable levels of cell death to control worms up until 9 days after RNAi, but significantly higher levels from 12 days and onward (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: Based on TUNEL quantification shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: mex3-1(RNAi) worms showed significantly increased levels of proliferation at every time point examined.
claims.source: We observed significantly increased levels of proliferation in mex3-1(RNAi) worms at every time point examined (Figure 4D), which suggested that stem cell division was not impeded by mex3-1 knockdown.
claims.evidence: Based on H3P immunolabeling quantification shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Worms pulsed with F-ara-EdU at 6 or 9 days after mex3-1 RNAi and fixed 24 hr later showed significantly increased numbers of total EdU-labeled cells compared to controls.
claims.source: Worms pulsed at either 6 or 9 days after RNAi and fixed 24 hr later showed significantly increased numbers of total EdU-labeled cells in mex3-1(RNAi) animals compared to controls (Figure 5A), demonstrating that during phenotypic progression, a greater number of cells were entering the cell cycle.
claims.evidence: Based on EdU labeling experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: FACS profiles of mex3-1(RNAi) animals at day 9 revealed relatively normal proportions of cells in both the X1 and X2 gates.
claims.source: FACS profiles of mex3-1(RNAi) animals at day 9 revealed relatively normal proportions of cells in both the X1 and X2 gates (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), further evidence that stem cells were progressing through the cell cycle and not arrested at 4C DNA in the X1 gate.
claims.evidence: Based on FACS analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Sublethally irradiated mex3-1(RNAi) worms expanded piwi-1+ stem cell numbers over time but produced disproportionately fewer prog-1+ progeny than control worms.
claims.source: Sublethally irradiated mex3-1(RNAi) worms expanded piwi-1+ stem cell numbers over time but produced disproportionately fewer prog-1+ progeny than control worms (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: Based on sublethal irradiation experiments and quantification shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: By 6 days after mex3-1 RNAi, there were highly significant increases in the number of piwi-1+ stem cells compared to controls, which rose to a 50% increase by day 12.
claims.source: By 6 days after RNAi, we observed highly significant increases in the number of piwi-1+ stem cells in mex3-1(RNAi) animals compared to controls, which rose to a 50% increase by day 12 (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Based on quantification of piwi-1+ cells in cross sections shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: All three neoblast subclasses (zeta, sigma, gamma) were significantly increased by approximately 50% in mex3-1(RNAi) animals at 12 days after RNAi.
claims.source: Assessment at 12 days after RNAi revealed that all three subclasses were significantly increased by approximately 50% in mex3-1(RNAi) animals compared to controls (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: Based on quantification of subclass markers shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: 7 days following EdU administration, numerous EdU+ cells were present in the epithelium of control(RNAi) worms, but virtually none had been incorporated into the epithelium in mex3-1(RNAi) animals.
claims.source: 7 days following EdU administration, numerous EdU+ cells were present in the epithelium of control(RNAi) worms, but virtually none had been incorporated into the epithelium in mex3-1(RNAi) animals (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: Based on EdU chase experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Following amputation, mex3-1(RNAi) worms failed to re-establish the expression of epithelial genes at wounding sites.
claims.source: Additionally, following amputation, mex3-1(RNAi) worms failed to re-establish the expression of epithelial genes at wounding sites, demonstrating that during both homeostasis and regeneration, mex3-1 is required for specification and differentiation of epithelial cell types (van Wolfswinkel et al., 2014) (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH analysis of regenerating blastemas shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: Quantification of lineage-restricted neoblast progeny in intact mex3-1(RNAi) worms 12 days after RNAi showed significant reductions in all examined cell types (chat, coe, ovo, FoxA, six1/2-2).
claims.source: Quantification of lineage-restricted neoblast progeny in intact mex3-1(RNAi) worms 12 days after RNAi showed significant reductions in all examined cell types (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: Based on quantification of PIWI-1+ cells co-expressing lineage markers shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Virtually all chat+PIWI-1+ cells expressed mex3-1.
claims.source: We observed that virtually all chat+PIWI-1+ cells expressed mex3-1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), suggesting a direct role for mex3-1 in regulating differentiation outside the epithelial lineage.
claims.evidence: Based on triple-label dFISH shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: 5 days following labeling with BrdU, the entry of new cells into brain, intestine, and pharynx was significantly decreased in mex3-1(RNAi) animals.
claims.source: Concordant with decreased production of lineage-restricted neoblast progeny, we also observed that 5 days following labeling with BrdU, the entry of new cells into brain, intestine, and pharynx was significantly decreased in mex3-1(RNAi) animals (Figure 6E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Based on BrdU chase experiments shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: Knockdown of p53 did not alter the numbers of PIWI-1+ovo+ eye- or PIWI-1+chat+ brain-specified neoblast progeny.
claims.source: We found that knockdown of p53 did not alter the numbers of PIWI-1+ovo+ eye- or PIWI-1+chat+ brain-specified neoblast progeny (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), demonstrating a broader role for mex3-1 in differentiation.
claims.evidence: Based on quantification in p53 RNAi animals shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: mex3-1 RNAi resulted in a significant increase in the number of piwi-1+PIWI-1+ cells and simultaneous decrease in piwi-1−PIWI-1+ cells compared to controls.
claims.source: We found that mex3-1 RNAi resulted in a significant increase in the number of piwi-1+PIWI-1+ cells and simultaneous decrease in piwi-1−PIWI-1+ cells compared to controls (Figure 6F), supporting a general reduction in the ability of stem cells to progress to a postmitotic state.
claims.evidence: Based on quantification of piwi-1 mRNA and PIWI-1 protein co-expression shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: 13/59 known stem cell-specific transcripts were significantly upregulated upon knockdown of mex3-1 (p < 0.01).
claims.source: In agreement with our data demonstrating hyper-proliferation and expansion of the entire stem cell compartment after mex3-1 knockdown, 13/59 known stem cell-specific transcripts were significantly upregulated upon knockdown of mex3-1 (p < 0.01, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: Based on RNAseq analysis of mex3-1 RNAi animals shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: An approximately 1.5-fold increase in soxP-1, zfp-1, and piwi-1 transcripts was observed in mex3-1(RNAi) animals.
claims.source: Importantly, we also observed an approximately 1.5-fold increase in soxP-1, zfp-1, and piwi-1 transcripts in mex3-1(RNAi) animals (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A; Supplementary file 4), concordant with the increase in stem cell subclasses quantified by cell counting (Figure 5C,D).
claims.evidence: Based on RNAseq data, consistent with cell counting results.

claims.claim: All but two of the new early and late progeny markers were severely down-regulated in the RNAseq data set for mex3-1(RNAi) animals compared to controls.
claims.source: As anticipated from the effects of mex3-1(RNAi) on the loss of all epithelial progenitor markers by WISH analyses, all but two of our new early and late progeny markers were severely down-regulated in the RNAseq data set for mex3-1(RNAi) animals compared to controls (Figure 7A; Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: Based on RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: The two transcripts that did not appreciably change after mex3-1 RNAi (sox9-1 and RPC-2) have very high X1 expression in addition to labeling epithelial progenitors.
claims.source: The two transcripts that did not appreciably change (sox9-1 and RPC-2) have very high X1 expression in addition to labeling epithelial progenitors, which was not expected to change in mex3-1 RNAi.
claims.evidence: Based on RNAseq data and expression patterns.

claims.claim: 20/21 down-regulated and uncharacterized transcripts produced a prog-like pattern in control worms and exhibited severely reduced expression in mex3-1(RNAi) worms.
claims.source: We found that 20/21 transcripts produced a prog-like pattern in control worms and exhibited severely reduced expression in mex3-1(RNAi) worms, as anticipated from RNAseq (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: Based on WISH validation of RNAseq candidates shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: SmedASXL_059179 was highly expressed near the proximal end of the pharynx, throughout the pharynx proper, and was similarly dependent on mex3-1 for its expression.
claims.source: The remaining transcript, SmedASXL_059179, was highly expressed near the proximal end of the pharynx, throughout the pharynx proper, and was similarly dependent on mex3-1 for its expression (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: Based on WISH analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: PIWI-1+SmedASXL_059179+ cells were observed near the proximal base of the pharynx.
claims.source: We predicted that SmedASXL_059179+ cells may represent a pharyngeal progenitor cell type, and indeed, we observed PIWI-1+SmedASXL_059179+ cells near the proximal base of the pharynx (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: Based on dFISH with PIWI-1 immunolabeling shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: RNAi against SmedASXL_059179 did not result in apparent perturbations to pharynx function during homeostasis or regeneration.
claims.source: However, no regulatory roles were uncovered for this gene, as RNAi against SmedASXL_059179 did not result in apparent perturbations to pharynx function during homeostasis or regeneration (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C,D).
claims.evidence: Based on RNAi experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Epithelial progenitors are the predominant output of stem cells, most likely reflecting highest turnover needs as well as molecular complexity of this organ.
claims.source: Combined with the revelation that zeta-neoblasts are the largest known lineage-restricted stem cell subclass in planarians, we conclude that epithelial progenitors are the predominant output of stem cells, most likely reflecting highest turnover needs as well as molecular complexity of this organ.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation based on the preponderance of epithelial markers found in the X2 fraction and known biology.

claims.claim: MEX3 is an RNA-binding translational repressor discovered in C. elegans with embryonic and post-embryonic developmental roles.
claims.source: MEX3 is an RNA-binding translational repressor discovered in C. elegans with embryonic and post-embryonic developmental roles (Draper et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature.

claims.claim: MEX3 is a fundamental regulator of asymmetry in C. elegans, mediating one of the earliest steps of cell fate determination by restricting expression of the cell fate determinant pal-1 transcription factor to the posterior blastomere of the early embryo.
claims.source: MEX3 is a fundamental regulator of asymmetry, mediating one of the earliest steps of cell fate determination in C. elegans by restricting expression of the cell fate determinant pal-1 transcription factor to the posterior blastomere of the early embryo (Draper et al., 1996; Huang et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature.

claims.claim: In adult C. elegans, MEX3 participates in the maintenance of germline stem cells (GSCs) by promoting proliferation, and is not required for GSCs to differentiate and undergo meiosis.
claims.source: In adult C. elegans, MEX3 participates in the maintenance of germline stem cells (GSCs) by promoting proliferation, and interestingly, is not required for GSCs to differentiate and undergo meiosis (Ariz et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature.

claims.claim: MEX3A overexpression increased levels of intestinal stem cell markers such as Bmi1 and Lgr5 in murine intestinal cell culture.
claims.source: Recent work on MEX3A in murine intestinal cell culture showed that the master intestinal differentiation factor Cdx2, one of the vertebrate homologs of pal-1, is a target of MEX3A translational inhibition, and furthermore, MEX3A overexpression increased levels of intestinal stem cell markers such as Bmi1 and Lgr5 (Pereira et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature.

claims.claim: The findings in planarians combined with results in C. elegans and vertebrates suggest a conserved ancestral function for mex3 genes in cell fate choice.
claims.source: Though the role of MEX3A in intestinal stem cell fate in vivo remains to be fully explored, these findings combined with our results in planarians suggest a conserved ancestral function for mex3 genes in cell fate choice.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparative analysis across species.

claims.claim: Unlike zfp-1(RNAi) worms, mex3-1(RNAi) worms completely lose the ability to form any regenerative blastema.
claims.source: Although both zfp-1 and mex3-1 are required for specification of epithelial-fated progeny, unlike zfp-1(RNAi) worms, mex3-1(RNAi) worms completely lose the ability to form any regenerative blastema.
claims.evidence: Based on comparison of regeneration phenotypes between the two RNAi conditions.

claims.claim: mex3-1 acts to mediate stem cell lineage asymmetry in the general stem cell pool and regulate all postmitotic lineages.
claims.source: mex3-1 was further needed to prevent the expansion of the stem cell compartment, including sigma-, gamma-, and zeta-class neoblasts, which suggests that mex3-1 acts to mediate stem cell lineage asymmetry in the general stem cell pool and regulate all postmitotic lineages.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation based on the broad effects observed across all neoblast subclasses.

claims.claim: Both C. elegans and vertebrate MEX3 proteins have been shown to be translational repressors.
claims.source: As both C. elegans and vertebrate MEX3 proteins have been shown to be translational repressors, it is likely that this molecular function has been conserved in planarians.
claims.evidence: This is based on established knowledge from the literature.

claims.claim: mex3-1 acts as a repressor of stem cell identity and self-renewal genes in postmitotic progenitors to promote differentiation.
claims.source: Thus, we propose a model of stem cell lineage progression with mex3-1 acting as a repressor of stem cell identity and self-renewal genes in postmitotic progenitors to promote differentiation (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the data and known MEX3 function.

claims.claim: No planarian homolog to the conserved MEX3 target Cdx2/pal-1 could be found in existing transcriptomes or genomic sequence.
claims.source: No planarian homolog to the conserved MEX3 target Cdx2/pal-1 could be found in existing transcriptomes or genomic sequence (Sánchez Alvarado et al., 2003; Robb et al., 2008; Abril et al., 2010; Sandmann et al., 2011; Labbe et al., 2012; Onal et al., 2012; Resch et al., 2012; Solana et al., 2012; Fernandes et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Based on BLAST searches against planarian sequence databases.

claims.claim: Transcriptional analysis of mex3-1(RNAi) animals may be a promising avenue to discover rare and novel progeny markers.
claims.source: With the evidence described in this study implicating mex3-1 as a regulator of multiple neoblast progeny for other tissues, transcriptional analysis of mex3-1(RNAi) animals may be a promising avenue to discover rare and novel progeny markers.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed future direction based on the utility demonstrated in this study.

claims.claim: The identification of SmedASXL_059179 as a pharyngeal marker with expression in PIWI-1+ cells demonstrates that lineage-restricted progeny are present outside the X1 and X2 gates.
claims.source: The identification of one of these transcripts as a pharyngeal marker with expression in PIWI-1+ cells demonstrates that lineage-restricted progeny are present outside the X1 and X2 gates and merits the investment of future efforts toward screening further WThighXlow genes that are regulated by mex3-1 in order to uncover novel progenitors.
claims.evidence: Based on the characterization of SmedASXL_059179 shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Smed-mex3-1 mediates asymmetric cell fate in planarian stem cell lineages, similar to MEX3's role in C. elegans embryogenesis.
claims.source: Due to the well-known function of MEX3 in mediating asymmetric cell fates during Caenorhabditis elegans embryogenesis (Draper et al., 1996), we propose that Smed-mex3-1 mediates a similar process in planarian stem cell lineages.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on functional conservation across species.

results.result: RNAseq analysis identified 2839 X1-enriched and 1512 X2-enriched transcripts (p ≤ 0.01), with X1 and X2 cells sharing the majority of their transcriptional profiles.
results.evaluation: Claims C4 and C5 are directly supported by DESeq analysis and hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 1. The statistical threshold is clearly stated, and the overlap in transcriptional profiles is demonstrated by the clustering analysis.

results.result: 32 new markers distinguish two main epithelial progenitor populations: 13 early progeny markers (lost by 48 hr post-irradiation) and 19 late progeny markers (lost beyond 48 hr post-irradiation).
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C23-C26 are well-supported by WISH analysis showing expression patterns and irradiation time-course experiments (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2). The kinetics of marker loss clearly distinguish early from late progeny populations.

results.result: dFISH quantification reveals minimal overlap between piwi-1+ stem cells and AGAT-1+ late progeny (0.29% ± 0.50), modest overlap between piwi-1 and prog-1+ early progeny (7.2% ± 2.1), and low overlap between prog-1+ and AGAT-1+ populations (5.4% ± 2.4).
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C33 are supported by quantitative dFISH experiments with standard deviations reported (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 3). The data contradict a previous study reporting 45% overlap, which the authors address explicitly. The measurements appear rigorous with appropriate replication.

results.result: All newly identified epithelial progenitor markers were down-regulated after zfp-1 RNAi, confirming their expression in epithelial progenitors.
results.evaluation: Claim C34 is supported by WISH analysis in zfp-1 RNAi animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 4). This validation is appropriate given that zfp-1 is known to specifically ablate epithelial progenitors, providing functional confirmation of marker identity.

results.result: prog-1 and prog-2 belong to a planarian-specific gene family of at least 24 members with no clear homology to other animals, containing only a predicted N-terminal signal sequence suggesting secretion.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C16-C18 are supported by BLAST searches, sequence alignment analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), and protein domain prediction. The lack of homology outside planarians is appropriately documented with searches against multiple flatworm genomes.

results.result: RNAi screening of epithelial progenitor markers revealed no detectable phenotypes, suggesting functional redundancy among these genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C36 are supported by RNAi screening experiments. The interpretation of functional redundancy is reasonable given the large gene family identified (24 members), though alternative explanations (e.g., incomplete knockdown, compensatory mechanisms) are not fully excluded.

results.result: mex3-1 RNAi was completely penetrant and lethal, causing ventral curling, head regression, dorsal lesioning during homeostasis, and complete loss of regenerative ability after amputation.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C38, C10 are supported by phenotypic observations and regeneration assays (Figure 3A-C). The phenotypes are clearly documented with survival curves and images showing 100% penetrance and lethality.

results.result: mex3-1 showed >5-fold enrichment in X2 over irradiated animals but also significant X1 expression, and was widely expressed in stem cells, early progeny, and late progeny by dFISH.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C41 are supported by RNAseq quantification (Figure 3D) and dFISH co-localization analysis (Figure 3F). The expression pattern is consistent with a gene functioning across multiple stages of the lineage.

results.result: mex3-1 knockdown leads to rapid decline of prog-1/2+ and AGAT-1+ progeny populations (majority lost by 6 days) but not stem cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C43, C11 are supported by time-course WISH analysis (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1). The selective loss of progeny without stem cell depletion is clearly demonstrated across multiple markers and time points.

results.result: mex3-1 RNAi animals showed comparable cell death to controls until day 9, but significantly increased proliferation (H3P+) and S-phase entry (EdU+) at all time points, with normal FACS profiles at day 9.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C47 are supported by TUNEL quantification (Figure 4C), H3P immunolabeling (Figure 4D), EdU labeling (Figure 5A), and FACS analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C). The data convincingly exclude cell cycle arrest as the cause of progeny loss.

results.result: mex3-1 knockdown caused expansion of piwi-1+ stem cells (50% increase by day 12) across all three neoblast subclasses (sigma, zeta, gamma), while sublethally irradiated mex3-1 RNAi animals produced disproportionately fewer prog-1+ progeny.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C50, C12-C13 are supported by quantification in cross sections (Figure 5C), subclass marker analysis (Figure 5D), and sublethal irradiation experiments (Figure 5B). The ~50% increase is consistent across multiple measurements and subclasses, with appropriate statistical testing.

results.result: mex3-1 RNAi animals showed virtually no EdU+ cell incorporation into epithelium after 7 days and failed to re-establish epithelial gene expression at wound sites during regeneration.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C52 are supported by EdU chase experiments (Figure 6A) and dFISH analysis of regenerating blastemas (Figure 6B). The data demonstrate impaired epithelial turnover during both homeostasis and regeneration.

results.result: mex3-1 knockdown caused significant reductions in lineage-restricted neoblast progeny for multiple tissues (chat+, coe+, ovo+, FoxA+, six1/2-2+) and decreased BrdU+ cell entry into brain, intestine, and pharynx.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C55 are supported by quantification of PIWI-1+ cells co-expressing lineage markers (Figure 6D), triple-label dFISH (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), and BrdU chase experiments (Figure 6E). The data demonstrate broad effects beyond the epithelial lineage.

results.result: p53 knockdown did not alter numbers of PIWI-1+ovo+ or PIWI-1+chat+ lineage-restricted progeny, demonstrating a broader role for mex3-1 in differentiation compared to p53.
results.evaluation: Claim C56 is supported by quantification in p53 RNAi animals (Figure 6—figure supplement 2). This control experiment appropriately distinguishes mex3-1 function from p53, which was previously shown to affect prog-1+ progeny.

results.result: mex3-1 RNAi resulted in significant increase in piwi-1+PIWI-1+ cells and simultaneous decrease in piwi-1−PIWI-1+ cells, supporting reduced ability to progress to postmitotic state.
results.evaluation: Claim C57 is supported by quantification of piwi-1 mRNA and PIWI-1 protein co-expression (Figure 6F). The shift from piwi-1−PIWI-1+ (postmitotic) to piwi-1+PIWI-1+ (stem cells) is consistent with the overall phenotype.

results.result: RNAseq of mex3-1 RNAi animals showed 13/59 known stem cell transcripts significantly upregulated (p < 0.01), including ~1.5-fold increases in soxP-1, zfp-1, and piwi-1.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C59 are supported by RNAseq analysis (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 4). The transcriptional changes are concordant with the observed expansion of stem cell subclasses by cell counting (Figure 5C,D).

results.result: All but two newly identified progeny markers (sox9-1, RPC-2) were severely down-regulated in mex3-1 RNAi animals by RNAseq, with 20/21 additional down-regulated transcripts validated by WISH showing prog-like patterns.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C63 are supported by RNAseq analysis (Figure 7A) and WISH validation (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C). The exceptions (sox9-1, RPC-2) are appropriately explained by their high X1 expression.

results.result: SmedASXL_059179 was identified as a pharyngeal marker with PIWI-1+ expression, demonstrating that lineage-restricted progeny exist outside the X1 and X2 FACS gates.
results.evaluation: Claims C64, C78 are supported by dFISH with PIWI-1 immunolabeling (Figure 7C). This finding is significant as it reveals limitations of the X1/X2 FACS approach for capturing all progenitor populations.

results.result: RNAi against SmedASXL_059179 did not result in apparent perturbations to pharynx function during homeostasis or regeneration.
results.evaluation: Claim C65 is supported by RNAi experiments (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C,D). However, the lack of phenotype may reflect functional redundancy, incomplete knockdown, or subtle defects not detected by the assays used.

results.result: mex3-1 functions to maintain asymmetry in stem cell lineage progression by promoting postmitotic fates and suppressing self-renewal, acting broadly across multiple lineages.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C8, C14-C15, C73 represent the central interpretation of the study. This model is well-supported by the combined data showing: (1) loss of multiple lineage progeny, (2) expansion of all stem cell subclasses, (3) increased proliferation, (4) impaired tissue turnover, and (5) loss of regenerative ability. The interpretation is logical and consistent with all observations.

results.result: Epithelial progenitors are the predominant output of stem cells, reflecting highest turnover needs and molecular complexity of this organ.
results.evaluation: Claim C66 is an inference supported by the preponderance of epithelial markers in the X2 fraction (32/80 detectable genes) and the known size of the zeta-neoblast subclass. The interpretation is reasonable given the data, though quantitative comparison of turnover rates across tissues would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: MEX3 is an RNA-binding translational repressor with conserved roles in asymmetric cell fate determination in C. elegans embryogenesis and adult germline, and in vertebrate intestinal stem cell regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C70 represent established knowledge from the literature, appropriately cited. These claims provide important context for interpreting the planarian mex3-1 results.

results.result: The findings in planarians combined with results in C. elegans and vertebrates suggest a conserved ancestral function for mex3 genes in cell fate choice and asymmetric cell fate determination.
results.evaluation: Claims C71, C79 represent a comparative inference based on functional similarities across species. The interpretation is reasonable given the conserved role in promoting differentiation and restricting stem cell identity, though direct molecular evidence for conserved mechanisms (e.g., shared targets) is lacking.

results.result: Unlike zfp-1 RNAi worms, mex3-1 RNAi worms completely lose the ability to form any regenerative blastema.
results.evaluation: Claim C72 is supported by comparison of regeneration phenotypes. This distinction is important as it suggests mex3-1 has broader effects than zfp-1, which specifically affects epithelial progenitors.

results.result: MEX3 proteins are translational repressors in C. elegans and vertebrates, suggesting mex3-1 acts as a repressor of stem cell identity and self-renewal genes in postmitotic progenitors to promote differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claim C74 is supported by literature, but C75 is a proposed model without direct experimental evidence. The model is plausible and consistent with the data, but the molecular mechanism (translational repression), specific targets, and whether MEX3-1 acts in stem cells vs. progeny remain to be demonstrated. This represents a testable hypothesis rather than a proven result.

results.result: No planarian homolog to the conserved MEX3 target Cdx2/pal-1 could be found in existing transcriptomes or genomic sequence.
results.evaluation: Claim C76 is supported by BLAST searches against planarian databases. This negative result is important as it suggests either divergent targets or that the homolog is highly diverged and not detectable by sequence similarity.

results.result: Transcriptional analysis of mex3-1 RNAi animals may be a promising avenue to discover rare and novel progeny markers.
results.evaluation: Claim C77 is a proposed future direction supported by the successful identification of 20/21 new progeny markers using this approach (C62). The utility of the method has been demonstrated in the current study.

results.result: Two other MEX3 homologs in S. mediterranea (mex3-2 and mex3-3) were neither irradiation-sensitive nor produced observable phenotypes after knockdown.
results.evaluation: Claim C39 is supported by RNAseq data and RNAi experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). This control is important for demonstrating specificity of mex3-1 function, though it's possible these homologs have redundant functions or roles in other contexts not tested.

results.result: Neoblasts are adult stem cells in planarians that sustain cell replacement during homeostasis and regeneration. The X1 FACS population is >90% piwi-1+ (stem cells), while X2 is 10-20% piwi-1+ (enriched for progeny).
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3 represent established background knowledge appropriately cited from previous studies. These foundational concepts are well-accepted in the field and provide necessary context.
